question: How much contract schema complexity can small/open models (<= 14B) tolerate before reasoning degrades? Addressed: small/open models (Q3-2026 small tier) gain +33.8% CUA and +22.3% SC when moving from a 1450-token monolithic contract to a 227-token progressive (Tier 1) contract. The frontier-tier gain is only +5.7%, confirming the asymmetry: progressive disclosure primarily rescues small models. 13 binding tests in tests/test_model_compatibility_q001.py pin this. Live confirmation against actual <=14B models is the next step (out of scope for protocol-freeze; the simulation in experiments/model_compatibility.py is deterministic and reproducible with seed=42).
target_phase: Phase D (resolved at protocol-freeze; live confirmation in STUDY-011 Phase 1)

question: What consistency model is required for multi-agent shared state (Strict Serializability vs Eventual Consistency)? Addressed by ADR-007: recommended Option D (Hybrid: Mission-state SS + World-state EC). Control plane (mission lifecycle, criteria, recovery) must be SS; data plane (workspace, env, agent) can be EC. Failure mode: consensus unavailable = fail-closed. Implementation phased through Phase 7-10. ADR-007 is at docs/architecture/ADR-007-state-consistency-q003.md.

How can RFC 8693 token exchange securely bind natural-language mission constraints to IAM policies? RESOLVED at design+implementation level: ADR-008 (docs/architecture/ADR-008-rfc8693-token-binding-q004.md) specifies a Mission Delegation Token chain with objective_hash + constraints_hash binding, monotonic attenuation (scope subset, depth cap, tau shrink), deny-list growth, and fail-closed verification. Implemented in delegation/token_exchange.py (pure stdlib+PyJWT, no network). 20 binding tests in tests/test_token_exchange_q004.py cover all 10 ADR-named classes (issue, exchange, attenuation, hash mismatch, expired, forged signature, depth overflow, purpose mismatch, deny-list precedence, tau monotonicity) plus TH-12 TOCTOU closure. Remaining: Phase 8 wiring into capabilities/dispatcher.py, IAM-side condition mapping validation in live environment (Q-011-gated).

What level of verification separation is sufficient to eliminate sycophantic confirmation bias? Addressed: LAB hardened in v0.3.3 (DEC-023) to use object-identity singleton check (`caller is AgentPrincipal`) as the primary defense, with the legacy name check as defense-in-depth. A hostile in-process Principal(name='AgentPrincipal') is now rejected. Pinned by tests/test_lab_class_identity_hardening.py (5 tests) and test_sycophancy_prevention.py::test_lab_uses_object_identity_hardening. Threat catalog TH-11 added to security/THREAT-MODEL-AND-SUPPLY-CHAIN.md.
target_phase: Phase G (resolved 2026-09-04; no further adversarial evaluation scheduled)

question: Does progressive disclosure in mission UI prevent information overload while preserving perceived control? Pilot-level support: GOMS/KLM simulation (seed=777, 64 personas x 4 tasks = 256 trials, N=0 humans) validates the measurement pipeline and direction: HEVO chat 6.59 -> mission 1.99 turns (~70% reduction), NASA-TLX lower, undetected errors lower in mission arm. Pinned by tests/test_study006_goms_pilot.py and tests/test_hci_cognitive_model_script.py (9 tests). SIMULATED only — live human subject trial (N>=30, IRB) remains the STUDY-006 preregistered next step.
